title: Evaluated pure reduction multiplication triangle
statement: Let ell be prime, W any scheme, D a diagonal derived reduction and eta its quotient-normalized evaluated units [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface, lem-sfb-diagonal-evaluation-unit]. Let M be any integral pro-etale sheaf and b:T(M[1])≅H[2] a supplied pure-system comparison. There are arrows d_n:U(H_n)→M such that (ell^(n+1), eta_n followed by the canonical evaluated comparison of b, single(d_n)[2] followed by shift addition) is a distinguished triangle on single(M)[1], and U(H_(n+1)→H_n) followed by d_n equals d_(n+1) followed by ell. No roots, finite Tate lines or Kummer classes occur.

source.place: Steps (2) and (3), the common two-term resolution and its (ell,1) transition.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution of M[1]. Nonzero integer multiplication is mono on its terms and exact p-adic extension preserves it. At level n identify the scalar-extended quotient with the integral quotient using Z_ell/ell^(n+1)=Z/ell^(n+1), compatibly with the quotient unit. The degreewise short exact sequence gives the multiplication triangle.

On this resolving class the supplied derived counit is invertible by uniqueness of the pointwise left-derived functor. The complexes equation for eta identifies the quotient arrow after transport to M[1]. Compose with the supplied b and exact evaluation comparisons. Full faithfulness of the single functor followed by shift two writes the last arrow uniquely as single(d_n)[2] followed by shift addition.

Use the same resolution at consecutive levels. The morphism of multiplication short exact sequences has components ell on the first object, identity on the second, and the quotient transition on the third. Naturality of their connecting arrows, transport by b, and faithfulness of shifted singles give the displayed equality for d_n. This proves naturality without detecting arbitrary derived arrows levelwise.
